jetty_water.summary:
JETTY (trip-critical): Private catamaran ferries in Port Blair / Sri Vijaya Puram depart from HADDO JETTY (Haddo Wharf), NOT Phoenix Bay. The strongest proof is Green Ocean's OWN e-ticket print portal (tickets.greenoceanseaways.com), whose tickets print the Port Blair terminal as "Haddo (Gate-3)" together with "Reporting time should be 01 hours prior to Departure." Makruzz's own FAQ likewise tells passengers to "reach Haddo Jetty" from the airport, and Makruzz's own blog states "Ferries usually depart from: Haddo Wharf, Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair)". Nautika's own site never names a jetty at all — it only says "the boarding point ... will be mentioned on your cruise ticket" — so for Nautika I rely on non-operator sources (all of which say Haddo). Phoenix Bay Jetty is the GOVERNMENT (DSS) ferry terminal (Havelock, Neil, Rangat, Diglipur, outer islands, plus Little Andaman mainline sailings); it is about 1 km from Haddo, in the same Port Blair harbour but a separate terminal/building. Reporting time: Green Ocean 60 min, Makruzz 60 min (check-in closes T-15, boarding closes T-10), Nautika 45 min (its FAQ says boarding closes T-15, its Terms say T-20 — a self-contradiction on Nautika's own site). For a 13:15 sailing, 11:55 arrival = 80 min before departure, comfortably inside every operator's rule.
BHARATPUR (Task 2): The "08:00–15:00" and "from Rs 3,500" figures the crew were worried about BOTH come from the same yellow callout box on go2andaman.com's Bharatpur page — and that box is the "Neil Island – Day Trip" tour package (it ends with "Book with us: Neil Island – Day Trip" and a booking button). It is NOT the watersports counter hours and NOT the snorkelling price. Refuted. Real picture: the beach itself is listed 05:00–18:00 daily, entry free; individual watersports counters run roughly 08:00–17:00 overall, with snorkelling ~09:00–16:00, glass-bottom boat ~08:00–16:00 and jet ski ~10:00–17:00. Walk-up snorkelling at the Bharatpur counter is ~Rs 500–1,000 pp; pre-booked online through agencies it is Rs 2,500–3,000 pp. Jet ski is a 10-minute single ride, Rs 500–700 pp. Glass-bottom boat Rs 400–800 pp.
SCUBA ON NEIL (Task 3): Three dive centres run dives from Neil itself — Turquoise Dream (near Neil Jetty, 5-min walk), India Scuba Explorers (Beach No.1, Neil's first PADI centre, est. 2007) and DIVEIndia's Neil DIVESchool (Dancing Dugong Resort, 100 m from jetty). Cheapest real beginner price on Neil from an operator's own site: Turquoise Dream "Discover Scuba Diving" Rs 5,500 pp (equipment, instruction, boat transfers, certification included; 10% off for groups of 4+). India Scuba Explorers: "Try Dive Lite" Rs 5,000 + 18% GST (= Rs 5,900) for a 1-hour/30-min-underwater program, or full "PADI DSD" Rs 7,000 + GST (= Rs 8,260), half day. DIVEIndia's beginner product on Neil is "Intro to Scuba", Rs 14,000 pp all-inclusive — but it is a 2-DAY, 2-DIVE program, not a single try dive, so it is not comparable. Late-September operation: Turquoise Dream says it dives "year-round (weather permitting)" with 7 AM dives; DIVEIndia says the best time is "All year round, dictated only by the Ocean's moods". Booking lead time on Neil: 2–3 days in peak season (Dec–Mar); same-day possible subject to availability — so 23–27 Sep is a low-pressure window.
MONSOON CAVEAT: 23–27 Sep 2026 falls at the tail of the SW monsoon. Every source agrees the "season" is Oct–May and that June–Sep activities "pause or run reduced hours" / "may be restricted" because of swell and visibility. Ferries themselves definitely run (Makruzz's live booking engine sells the 08:00 Port Blair→Neil sailing for 23 Sep 2026 at Rs 1,950 Premium, 88 seats free), but boat-based watersports at Bharatpur on a given day are weather-dependent. No source states a fixed September closure date.
SOURCE-KIND NOTE: greenoceanseaways.com's public pages carry NO jetty or reporting-time information at all (its FAQ and Contact links are dead, and its published schedule page is stale, headed "SCHEDULE OPEN FOR 01 MAY 2024 - 15 AUGUST 2024"). The Haddo/1-hour evidence for Green Ocean therefore comes from Google's cached snippet of Green Ocean's own ticket-print portal, not from a page I could open directly (the ticket URLs 404 now, and I deliberately did not attempt to view other travellers' ticket data). A&N government sites (dss.andaman.gov.in, andamantourism.gov.in) could NOT be opened — the browser extension denied content access on those domains — so no government-sourced confirmation was obtainable.

critical_claims.claim: THE JETTY: Green Ocean's private catamarans depart Port Blair from HADDO JETTY, Gate 3 — not Phoenix Bay. Green Ocean's own e-ticket prints the Port Blair terminal as "Haddo (Gate-3)" and instructs "Reporting time should be 01 hours prior to Departure." The crew should go to Haddo Jetty (Haddo Wharf), the blue 'Passenger Terminal' gate off the Haddo road, ~4 km / 15-20 min from IXZ airport, and be there by 12:15 for a 13:15 sailing — an 11:55 arrival is correct and gives 20 min of slack. Makruzz's own FAQ independently says "...to reach Haddo Jetty" and Makruzz's own blog says "Ferries usually depart from: Haddo Wharf, Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair)". Phoenix Bay Jetty, about 1 km away in the same harbour, is the GOVERNMENT (DSS) ferry terminal — different building, tickets sold at the counter. Nautika's own site names no jetty (only "the boarding point ... will be mentioned on your cruise ticket"); all non-operator sources put Nautika at Haddo too. One dissenting source (andamanislands.com, a travel agency) says "Ferries to Neil Island operate from Phoenix Bay Jetty" — it is wrong for private ferries and is outranked by the operator's own printed ticket.

BHARATPUR COUNTER HOURS: The "08:00-15:00" claim is REFUTED as watersports hours — verified on-page, that figure (together with "from Rs 3,500") sits inside go2andaman.com's "Neil Island - Day Trip" package callout box, which ends with a "Book Neil Island Day Trip" button. The actual position: Bharatpur Beach itself is listed 5:00 AM - 6:00 PM daily, entry free; the watersports counters run roughly 8 AM to 5 PM, with snorkelling 9 AM - 4 PM, glass-bottom boat 8 AM - 4 PM and jet ski 10 AM - 5 PM. A Thursday-afternoon plan therefore works, but arrive by ~14:00-14:30 to be safe: snorkelling's last slot is around 15:00-16:00 and morning has the calmer water. In late September (tail of monsoon) individual boat-based activities can be suspended on the day for sea conditions.

CHEAPEST REAL BEGINNER SCUBA ON NEIL: Rs 5,500 per person — Turquoise Dream's "Discover Scuba Diving in Neil Island", stated on the operator's own site, including equipment, instruction, boat transfers and certification, with a 10% group discount for 4+ (so no discount for a party of 3). Runner-up from an operator's own site: India Scuba Explorers' "Try Dive Lite", Rs 5,000 + 18% GST = Rs 5,900 (1 hour, 30 min underwater, max 12 m); their full PADI DSD is Rs 7,000 + GST = Rs 8,260 (half day, 1 dive). Do NOT quote DIVEIndia's Rs 14,000 as a try-dive price — that is their 2-day, 2-dive "Intro to Scuba" program (Havelock & Neil, same price). Bharatpur beach counters advertise boat scuba from ~Rs 3,500-4,500, but no operator's own site backs that figure. Turquoise Dream confirms it dives "year-round (weather permitting)" with 7 AM starts and asks only 2-3 days' notice in peak season (Dec-Mar), with same-day possible — so late September is bookable at short notice.

warnings: Green Ocean's public website carries NO jetty or reporting-time information at all — its footer FAQ (faqs.html) and Contact (contact.html) links are dead and silently fall back to the homepage. The Haddo (Gate-3) / 1-hour reporting evidence for Green Ocean comes from Google's cached snippet of Green Ocean's OWN ticket-print portal (tickets.greenoceanseaways.com), not from a page I could open live — the two indexed ticket URLs now return 404. I also deliberately did not pursue those URLs further because they contain other travellers' personal booking data.

Green Ocean's published schedule page is badly out of date: it is headed "SCHEDULE OPEN FOR 01 MAY 2024- 31 MAY 2024" and "SCHEDULE OPEN FOR 01 JUNE 2024 - 15 AUGUST 2024". I could NOT verify the 13:15 Green Ocean sailing on 23 Sep 2026 anywhere on Green Ocean's own site: their booking portal returned "No seat available on this day" for Port Blair->Neil on 23-09-2026, and returned the same message for a control search (Port Blair->Havelock, 24-08-2026), which suggests the portal is not serving schedules rather than the sailing being full. Re-confirm the 13:15 departure and the Haddo Gate-3 reporting point directly on the e-ticket, or by phone on +91-03192-230777 / info@greenoceancruise.com, before travel.

Nautika contradicts itself on its own site about boarding cut-off: the FAQ says "boarding closes 15 minutes prior to departure" while the Terms of Service say "boarding closes 20 min before departure". Use the stricter 20-minute figure. Nautika's FAQ text also still refers customers to "SeaLink customer care" rather than Nautika.

A&N government sources could NOT be checked: navigation to dss.andaman.gov.in and www.andamantourism.gov.in was allowed but the browser extension returned "Permission denied for reading page content on this domain", so no Directorate of Shipping Services or A&N Administration page could be read. The jetty allocation is therefore evidenced by operator documents and travel-trade sources only, with no government confirmation.

Bharatpur watersports prices are counter/on-the-day prices with no single authoritative source. Snorkelling ranges from "from Rs 500" (andamantourism.org) to "Rs 1,000" (andamantourism.org.in) to Rs 2,500-3,000 if pre-booked online through an agency; jet ski ranges Rs 500-700 for the same 10-minute ride; glass-bottom boat Rs 400-800. Expect to negotiate at the counter and expect the figures to differ from anything published.

India Scuba Explorers' website footer reads "© 2020" and its content shows no sign of recent updating, so its Rs 5,000 / Rs 7,000 try-dive prices (plus 18% GST) may be stale. Turquoise Dream's footer reads "© 2003-2024" and several of its own internal links 404 (e.g. /dive-programs/discover-scuba-diving), so its Rs 5,500 figure — which I read from its live homepage FAQ — should also be reconfirmed by WhatsApp before relying on it.

23-27 Sep 2026 sits at the tail end of the southwest monsoon. Every source, including the operators, treats Oct-May as the season; June-Sep activities "pause or run reduced hours" and "may be restricted". Ferries themselves are running (Makruzz's live engine sells the 08:00 Port Blair->Neil sailing for 23 Sep 2026), but snorkelling, glass-bottom boat, jet ski and boat scuba at Bharatpur are decided on the day by sea state. Build a rain/rough-sea fallback into the Thursday afternoon plan and do not prepay non-refundable watersports.

The Andaman Bliss snorkelling page contradicts itself on age limits: the booking panel says "Age Limit: 10 to 55 years" while its own FAQ says "The minimum age for snorkeling is 12 years and above." Confirm at the counter if anyone in the party is near those bounds.

Nothing on any operator site addresses vegetarian catering for the 3 vegetarian adults; Makruzz's T&Cs only mention a "snack box" for Deluxe/Royal class and Nautika mentions a snack kiosk. Meal suitability was not verifiable and should be checked directly.

land_ops.summary:
All four tasks researched by opening pages in Chrome (no WebFetch/WebSearch). Tab 1977593512 was created for this work and closed at the end. Tabs 1977593503 and 1977593515 belong to other sessions and were left untouched.

TASK 1 — BARATANG DAY TRIP, Sat 26 Sep 2026, 3 vegetarian adults from Port Blair.
The conflicting prices resolve into two different cost MODELS, not two prices for the same thing:
(a) PRIVATE CAB (vehicle-priced). Dekho Andaman (local operator, Port Blair, +91 7063-950-125) publishes the cleanest breakdown: Ertiga SUV (max 6 pax + driver) round trip Port Blair↔Baratang with Limestone Cave + Mud Volcano = ₹5,400 (9 hrs); Limestone Cave only = ₹4,800 (8 hrs). INCLUDED in that ₹5,400: cab+driver all day, parking and toll charges, VEHICLE FERRY TICKETS at Middle Strait, professional driver, "Permit for Middle Andaman for every Traveler". EXCLUDED: any meals, and the Limestone Cave speedboat at ₹800/person extra. So for 3 adults: ₹5,400 + 3×₹800 = ₹7,800 (≈₹2,600 pp) before food. A sedan (Dzire/Etios, 2–3 pax) is the right size for 3 and e-Andaman Tourism lists ₹5,000–₹6,500 for that round trip; ferrybooking.in (Port Blair) lists ₹5,400 for max 4 pax; Tropical Andamans ₹4,000–6,000/vehicle; Andaman Ocean ₹4,500 approx; TravelTriangle ₹4,500–6,000. So a realistic private-cab figure for 3 people is ₹4,500–6,500 for the CAR, plus ~₹800–900 pp boat, plus ~₹10–14 pp vehicle ferry if not included, plus food = roughly ₹7,000–9,500 total for the three (₹2,350–3,200 pp).
(b) SHARED / JOINING TOUR (per-head). Andaman Ocean (Port Blair operator since 2013): ₹2,250 pp sharing, including A/C shared cab hotel pickup-drop, convoy permit assistance at Jirkatang, shared speedboat tickets, entry-permit/ticket coordination, tolls and parking, trip coordinator. Explicitly EXCLUDED: vehicle ferry ticket ₹14/pp, all meals, professional cave guide (extra on request), camera fees, forest entry charges not listed, Mud Volcano add-on, GST if applicable. Same operator's second page and their own T&C quote ₹2,100 pp — an internal inconsistency on their own site. Other per-head quotes: Tropical Andamans ₹1,500–2,500 pp all-in; e-Andaman Tourism ₹2,500–4,000 pp "shared tour/coach"; TravelTriangle ₹1,000–1,500 pp bare shared and ₹3,000–3,500 pp for a full operator package. For 3 adults sharing: ~₹6,300–7,500 total. Verdict: for exactly 3 people the private cab and the shared tour land in the same ballpark (~₹2,300–2,600 pp), so the private cab is the better buy — you get door-to-door control, no strangers, and the convoy-slot flexibility.
COMPONENTS: vehicle ferry across Middle Strait ₹10–14 pp (trivially cheap; included by some operators). Speedboat at Nilambur jetty ₹800–₹1,000 pp is the real consensus (Dekho Andaman ₹800; Andaman Ocean, ferrybooking.in and TravelTriangle ₹900; TravelTriangle table ₹900–1,000; e-Andaman ₹800–1,200/₹800–1,500; iAndaman's ₹600 is from a 2017-copyright page and is stale). PERMITS: Indian nationals need NO paid permit — you register with a government photo ID at the Jirkatang forest check post and the operator/driver handles the convoy paperwork (TravelTriangle, Tropical Andamans and e-Andaman Tourism all say this; Dekho Andaman bundles "Permit for Middle Andaman" into the cab price). Foreign nationals need a permit obtained in Port Blair. GUIDE: not in the base price — Andaman Ocean lists "Professional guide at Limestone Caves (available on request at extra cost)" as an exclusion, while Tropical Andamans says guides are mandatory at the caves and volcanoes and are handled by the operator. BREAKFAST/LUNCH: excluded by every operator without exception. CAVE ENTRY: sources disagree — TravelTriangle states flatly "No entry fee to the caves"; ferrybooking.in says ₹5–10 pp at the entry; Andaman Ocean bundles unspecified "entry tickets". Budget ₹10 pp and don't worry about it.
WALK AND TIME INSIDE: boat drop to cave entrance is ~1.2 km one way on a marked forest trail (Tropical Andamans, Exclusive Andaman), quoted up to 1.5–2 km by others; 15–20 min (Exclusive Andaman), 30–40 min (e-Andaman), Andaman Ocean warns off anyone who can't manage a 2–3 km round-trip walk. Time inside: 45–60 minutes (Tropical Andamans), 20–30 min (e-Andaman); Dekho Andaman allots 2 hours for the whole boat+trek+cave block, matching TravelTriangle's "~2 hours including boat + trek".
RETURN CONVOY (the 12:00 / 12:30 / 14:30 conflict): all three numbers appear, and they are describing DIFFERENT slots of a multi-departure schedule, not competing claims about one departure. Northbound from Jirkatang the schedule is very consistently 06:00, 09:00, 12:00 (or 12:30) and 14:30 (or 15:00/15:30). Southbound from the Baratang/Middle Strait side, Go2Andaman says 12:00 PM and 3:00 PM; Tropical Andamans (re-checked 27 July 2026) says "the last return at 3:00 PM"; Exclusive Andaman lists the fourth convoy at 3:00 PM; TravelTriangle's table lists ~12:00 PM, 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM; Localpostit reports 06:30/09:30/12:30/15:30 from the Mid Strait check post (i.e. offset ~30 min from Jirkatang). Dekho Andaman's hour-by-hour plan has the convoy leaving the Baratang side after lunch and reaching Jirkatang by 15:30, hotel by 17:00. PLANNING ANSWER: aim for the 06:00 Jirkatang convoy (pickup 03:30–04:30) and be back at the Middle Strait vehicle-ferry queue by ~13:00 to make the early-afternoon return; treat ~15:00 as the hard last convoy and do not cut it fine. Confirm the exact slots locally the day before — every operator says timings are periodically revised.
NOT AVAILABLE ON 26 SEP: Makruzz's new MV Makruzz Pearl Port Blair→Baratang ferry (05:45→07:45, ~₹2,300 Premium, no convoy, no permit) starts 1 October 2026, and in any case has no return sailing to Port Blair — it continues to Havelock at noon.

TASK 2 — FOOD.
AT NILAMBUR/BARATANG JETTY: yes, and vegetarian is easy. Go2Andaman's dedicated Baratang restaurants page names two: Mahima Restaurant (on the main road in Nilambur, left-hand side coming from the jetty) serving poori and paratha at breakfast, rice at lunch, with curries, veg sauces and salad, "packed with locals", cheap; and Preethi Restaurant (right-hand side of the main road from Nilambur jetty) serving thalis with vegetarian or seafood sides and vegetable biryani on request, with staff happy to refill your plate. Plus food stalls all around the jetty doing South Indian and Bengali dishes, chai, snacks, coconut water, spiced cucumber, buttermilk and lassi. Tropical Andamans: "Basic local restaurants operate near the jetty and in Baratang town — simple Indian food, perfectly decent. Options are limited." Their own trip photos are captioned "The jetty stalls — samosas, chai". e-Andaman Tourism: "simple dhabas near the jetty: veg thalis, omelettes, snacks, tea, fresh coconuts... hygiene and options are basic". PRICE: ₹150–350 per person for a simple lunch at the Baratang jetty (e-Andaman Tourism); the same site budgets ₹200–500 pp for meals/snacks across the day. Dekho Andaman's plan says "Have lunch from the Restaurants nearby or on the way back". Note ATMs and card acceptance are limited — carry small cash.
PORT BLAIR BEFORE 04:00: nothing is open. Go2Andaman's 2026 Port Blair restaurant round-up shows the earliest openings in town are 6:30 AM (Rajasthani Bhojnalay/Dhaba) and 7:00 AM (Annapurna in Aberdeen Bazaar — pure vegetarian, South Indian, ~₹500 for 2; also Javitri, also Buzzing Bee), and it explicitly notes "most places in Port Blair close down quite early", with the latest closer being Frywings at 11:30 PM. So carrying food from the previous night is effectively the only self-service option — but you should not need to: the standard operator practice is a hotel packed breakfast. Dekho Andaman's published tour plan states "Early morning at 4.00 am we start for BARATANG... This day you will be given have packed breakfast from the hotel." e-Andaman Tourism advises "Carry packed breakfast or grab tea and snacks near Jirkatang." Dekho Andaman also confirms you can refresh with tea and snacks at the Jirkatang check post while the driver does the paperwork (~05:00–06:00), and Luxury Andamans' sample plan has breakfast on arrival at Baratang around 08:00. RECOMMENDATION: ask the hotel the night before for a 03:30 packed breakfast, carry fruit/biscuits/water, and count on chai at Jirkatang.

TASK 3 — CELLULAR JAIL LIGHT & SOUND SHOW, SATURDAY 26 SEP 2026. Answered from the OFFICIAL government e-Tourist portal (tourism.andamannicobar.gov.in/etourist), linked from the official A&N Tourism homepage.
Three shows daily: 5:50 PM Hindi (all days), 6:50 PM Hindi (Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun), 6:50 PM ENGLISH (Mon/Wed/Fri only), 7:50 PM Hindi (all days). On Saturday 26 Sep 2026 ALL THREE SHOWS ARE IN HINDI — there is no English show on a Saturday. The claim that English runs only Mon/Wed/Fri is CONFIRMED, and doubly so: the portal's live seat-availability grid for the next 7 days shows "No Show" against the 06:50 PM English column on Thursday 20, Saturday 22, Sunday 23 and Tuesday 25 August 2026, and shows English available with the 06:50 PM Hindi marked "No Show" on Friday 21, Monday 24 and Wednesday 26 August. The pattern is hard-coded to the weekday.
Price: ₹300 per adult, ₹150 per child aged 5–11. For 3 adults = ₹900. This is a SEPARATE ticket from daytime museum entry (₹30 per Indian, ₹100 per foreigner). Photography charges: ₹200 per non-professional video/handy camera, ₹1,000 per professional video camera, ₹10,000/day for film shooting on the freedom movement with prior permission.
Where to buy: online on the official Andaman Tourism e-Tourist portal — register (name, age, gender, nationality, ID type and number, contact), get an acknowledgement number, pick services, pick date and show, pay via SBI ePay, print/save the confirmation slip. The portal also has Search Booking, Check Seat Availability and Verify Payment. I did not log in, register or pay. I found no published statement about an on-site counter or about how far in advance booking opens — the availability grid only publishes 7 days ahead, so 26 Sep 2026 seats are not yet listed as of 20 Aug 2026.
Bonus: the daytime Cellular Jail museum is open 9:00 AM–12:30 PM and 1:30 PM–5:00 PM, Tuesday to Sunday, closed Mondays and national holidays — so it is open on Sat 26 Sep. Note the museum's Monday closure does NOT stop the Monday evening shows.

TASK 4 — MUNDA PAHAD TREK, CHIDIYA TAPU.
TRAIL LENGTH: 1.5 km one way is the consensus. No source I opened says 1.3 km. Acquaint Andaman says "approx. 1.5 to 2 km (one way)". AndamansGuide's FAQ: "approximately 1.5 km long, starting from Chidiya Tapu Beach". andamantourism.org: "about 1.5 km one way".
TIME UP: genuinely varies by source and by fitness, 30–60 minutes one way. Fast end: AndamansGuide 30–40 min; Acquaint Andaman "a mild 30–40 minute hike". Slow end: andamantourism.org "roughly 45 to 60 minutes... the path is uneven with a few inclines, shaded most of the way"; Experience Andamans (Port Blair operator, enlisted with Ministry of Tourism) "approximately 40–60 minutes, and that depends on how fast you are". Both figures are right — 30 min is a brisk fit walker, 45–60 min is a normal pace with photo stops. Budget 2–2.5 hours round trip including time at the cliff.
ENTRY CUT-OFF: 15:00 CONFIRMED by two independent sources. AndamansGuide states "Entry for the trek closes at 3:00 PM, and visitors must return by 4:15–4:30 PM", and repeats it in its FAQ: "The Munda Pahad Trek timing is limited for safety. Entry closes at 3:00 PM, and visitors need to return by 4:15–4:30 PM." Acquaint Andaman's fact box lists "Timings: Approx. 1.5 to 2 km (one way) Till 03:00 PM". Caveat: neither is a government source and I found no forest-department notification online, so treat 15:00 as the working rule and confirm at the Chidiya Tapu forest check post on the day. Acquaint Andaman adds: "Trek only during daylight hours; avoid visiting after dark for safety."
CHIDIYA TAPU SUNSET RULES AND FEES: the beach and sunset point are FREE to enter (andamantourism.org, stated twice including in its FAQ; AndamansGuide also lists Munda Pahad entry as free). The beach "runs on daylight, roughly sunrise to sunset, and the forest road winds down after dark" — you're expected to leave once the light goes; there is little lighting on the forest road, mobile network is patchy to non-existent, and nothing is hireable out there after dark, so fix your cab's return and waiting time before you set off. Arrive at least 30 minutes before listed sunset for the good spots. Swimming is not advised — rocky seabed, strong currents, and saltwater crocodiles reported along the coast. Do NOT confuse two places: Chidiya Tapu Beach (the long rocky stretch you reach first) is the main sunset viewpoint; Munda Pahar Beach is a few km further and is where the trek starts. The Chidiya Tapu Biological Park is a separate ticketed forest-department facility: ₹20 per Indian visitor and ₹50 per foreign national with under-5s free per andamantourism.org, or "from ₹50 adults, ₹20 children" per Go2Andaman — sources disagree on the exact figure; 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, closed Mondays, camera charges extra (₹50 still / ₹100 video per Go2Andaman). Cab from Port Blair: ~25–28 km, 45–60 min drive, roughly ₹1,500 return for a sedan; government bus ~₹30 one way but infrequent and won't wait. Food at Chidiya Tapu is only small stalls near the parking area (tea, packaged snacks, coconut water) — no restaurants at the beach and none on the trail.

facts.topic: Baratang — hour-by-hour day plan with return convoy timing
facts.value: 04:00 AM start from Port Blair; packed breakfast from the hotel; Jirkatang check post — paperwork by driver, tea and snacks available; convoy reaches Middle Strait Port by 8:30 AM; ferry at 9:00 AM, Baratang in 20 minutes; speedboat to Limestone Cave; 2 hours at the cave; back in the boat around 12:00 PM; back at Baratang by 12:30 noon; lunch at nearby restaurants; Mud Volcano 5 km north; ferry back to Middle Strait; convoy restarts to Jirkatang guided by police vans, reaching Jirkatang by 3:30 PM; another 2 hours to the hotel, arriving 5:00 PM.

facts.topic: Baratang — outlier convoy claim
facts.value: Dekho Andaman's 'Things to Note' bullet states 'There are two convoys : 8.00 am and 10.00 am', which contradicts every other source including that same page's own hour-by-hour plan (which has the convoy reaching Middle Strait by 8:30 AM after a 4:00 AM start). Treat as an error on their page.

facts.topic: Baratang — full-day timeline with the vehicle-ferry leg
facts.value: 03:45–04:30 depart Port Blair for Jirkatang (40–45 km, 1–1.25 hrs); 05:30–06:30 queue, register, join the first convoy; 06:30–08:00 escorted convoy to Middle Strait/Nilambur Jetty (45–50 km); 08:00–08:30 vehicle ferry across Middle Strait to the Baratang side (wait time can vary); 08:45–10:45 speedboat + guided walk to the caves; 11:00–12:30 jeep and short hike to Mud Volcano; 12:45–13:30 simple lunch at Baratang jetty eateries plus buffer for the ferry/convoy; 13:30–15:30 return ferry and afternoon convoy; 16:30–17:30 back in Port Blair.

facts.topic: Baratang — per-group and per-person cost model
facts.value: Typical day-trip costs per group: private cab (sedan) ₹5,000–₹6,500; boat to Limestone Caves (shared) ₹800–₹1,200 pp; Mud Volcano local transfer ₹100–₹300 pp; permits/jetty/ferry ₹100–₹400 pp (some fees may be per vehicle); meals/snacks ₹200–₹500 pp. Sample per-person cost: 2 travellers sharing a sedan ≈₹3,000–₹4,000 pp; 4 travellers sharing an SUV ≈₹1,800–₹2,600 pp. Elsewhere on the same site: private cab full day ₹6,000–₹10,000 per vehicle; shared tour/coach ₹2,500–₹4,000 including convoy logistics; simple lunch at Baratang jetty ₹150–₹350.

facts.topic: Baratang — indicative all-in day-trip prices
facts.value: 'Group day tours run roughly ₹1,500–2,500 per person all-in as an indicative range; a private car roughly ₹4,000–6,000 per vehicle. Guides are mandatory at the caves and volcanoes; permits are handled by the operator.' FAQ: 'group day tours around ₹1,500–2,500 per person including transport, permits and boat rides; a private car around ₹4,000–6,000 per vehicle. Add a little for lunch and the optional Parrot Island boat.'

facts.topic: Baratang — private cab and packaged tour price ranges (aggregator view)
facts.value: 'A private cab round trip from Port Blair to Baratang costs roughly ₹4,500-₹6,000 for the car, shared among everyone travelling. You still pay about ₹900 per person for the speedboat.' 'A bundled Baratang day tour typically costs ₹1,000-₹1,500 per person at the shared level and up to about ₹3,000-₹3,500 for a full operator package.' Mud Volcano and Parrot Island each carry a small permit/boat charge of around ₹50 per person, usually not included.

facts.topic: Baratang — new Makruzz ferry (NOT available 26 Sep 2026)
facts.value: From 1 October 2026 MV Makruzz Pearl runs Port Blair 5:45 AM → Baratang 7:45 AM, ~₹2,300 in Premium, with no convoy, no reserve crossing and no permit needed. But it does not come back: at 12:00 PM the same vessel continues to Havelock, arriving 1:30 PM, and there is no sailing back to Port Blair. Irrelevant for a 26 September round trip.

facts.topic: Food at Nilambur/Baratang jetty — named restaurants and cuisine
facts.value: 'There aren't any fancy restaurants in Baratang, but you won't stay hungry either. A couple of food stalls and small eateries are dotted around the Nilambur jetty and mainly serve South Indian and Bengali dishes. You can find refreshments, snacks, and chai almost on every corner... very pocket-friendly.' MAHIMA RESTAURANT — by the main road in Nilambur, left-hand side coming from the jetty; poori and paratha for breakfast, rice for lunch, bread for dinner, all with typical curries, veg sauces and salad; packed with locals; cheap. PREETHI RESTAURANT — right-hand side of the main road from the Nilambur jetty; tasty thalis with vegetarian or seafood sides; can prepare biryani with chicken or vegetables. Also coconut water, spiced cucumbers, buttermilk and lassi from street vendors; cookies and chocolate from small shops.

facts.topic: Food at Baratang — veg options and price
facts.value: 'Lunch: Simple thalis (veg/egg/fish), fried snacks, coconuts at Baratang jetty stalls.' 'Simple lunch at Baratang jetty: INR 150–350 [per person].' Elsewhere on the same site: 'Expect simple dhabas near the jetty: veg thalis, omelettes, snacks, tea, fresh coconuts. Seafood availability varies; hygiene and options are basic—carry snacks and water.' Shopping/kiosks: 'Very limited. Small kiosks sell beverages, chips, seasonal fruits.'

facts.topic: Food at Baratang — operator's own read
facts.value: 'Basic local restaurants operate near the jetty and in Baratang town — simple Indian food, perfectly decent. Options are limited, so we carry snacks and water, and most tour packages include a lunch arrangement.' Their trip photo from the circuit is captioned 'The jetty stalls — samosas, chai, and the day's plan.'

facts.topic: Port Blair — earliest restaurant opening times (nothing before 04:00)
facts.value: Earliest openings among Port Blair's best-known restaurants: Rajasthani Bhojnalay / Rajasthani Dhaba 6:30 AM–10 PM (₹400 for 2); Annapurna, Aberdeen Bazaar 7 AM–10 PM, pure vegetarian, South Indian, 'opens early' (₹500 for 2); Javitri, School Line 7 AM–10 PM (pure veg main course, chaat, ₹250 for 2); The Buzzing Bee by Bayleaf Inn 7 AM–10 PM; Anju Coco, Aberdeen Bazaar 8 AM–10:30 PM; Lazeez 8 AM–3 PM and 6–11 PM; Icy Spicy (best vegetarian restaurant) 11 AM–10 PM. The page explicitly notes 'most places in Port Blair close down quite early', with Frywings the latest at 11:30 PM. Nothing opens before 04:00.

facts.topic: Pre-04:00 food solution — hotel packed breakfast is standard
facts.value: Operator's published tour plan: 'Early morning at 4.00 am we start for BARATANG island which is located 100 km towards the north of Port Blair. This day you will be given have packed breakfast from the hotel.' And: 'You will reach Jirgatang Check post. Here the paper works will be done by our drivers and you can refresh yourself with tea and snacks.' Also 'Breakfast and Lunch cab [can] be done from the Baratang Jetty.'

facts.topic: Pre-04:00 food — carry it or grab tea at Jirkatang
facts.value: 'Breakfast: Carry packed breakfast or grab tea and snacks near Jirkatang.' 'Hydration: Bring sufficient water; shade can be limited on trails.' Also 'Carry government ID, cash (ATMs and card acceptance are limited), water, snacks, and small change for local transfers.'

facts.topic: Munda Pahad — trail length, time and 15:00 entry cut-off
facts.value: 'This short 1.5 km trek takes about 30–40 minutes.' Key features: Entry Fee — Free. Timing — 'Entry for the trek closes at 3:00 PM, and visitors must return by 4:15–4:30 PM.' FAQ: 'The Munda Pahad trek is approximately 1.5 km long, starting from Chidiya Tapu Beach, and takes around 30 minutes to reach the viewpoint.' FAQ: 'The Munda Pahad Trek timing is limited for safety. Entry closes at 3:00 PM, and visitors need to return by 4:15–4:30 PM.' Food: 'There are no food stalls at the Munda Pahad viewpoint, but visitors can enjoy snacks from stalls at Chidiya Tapu beach nearby.'

facts.topic: Munda Pahad — 15:00 cut-off, second confirming source
facts.value: Fact box: 'Location: Near Chidiya Tapu, 25 km from Port Blair. Timings: Approx. 1.5 to 2 km (one way) Till 03:00 PM.' Trail description: 'The trail to Munda Pahad begins at the Chidiya Tapu forest check post. It's a mild 30–40 minute hike through thick coastal forest... The path is well-marked and suitable for beginners.' Travel tips: 'No shops or restrooms on the trail; use facilities at Chidiya Tapu Beach before starting' and 'Trek only during daylight hours; avoid visiting after dark for safety.'

facts.topic: Munda Pahad — longer time estimate (45–60 min) and terrain
facts.value: 'A moderate walk of about 1.5 km one way, roughly 45 to 60 minutes, runs through dense forest to a high point above the sea at the southern tip. The path is uneven with a few inclines, shaded most of the way. At the top you get an open view of the Bay of Bengal, with Rutland Island across Duncan Passage to the south... Wear proper shoes and start with enough daylight to get back.'

facts.topic: Munda Pahad — operator-run guided trek price and duration
facts.value: 'Trekking to Munda Pahad, Chidiatapu' — ₹1,500 per person, includes climbing and cab. 'We start around 1:30 PM from your hotel to Chidiyatapu... around 30 KM from the main city... journey would take around one hour.' 'The trekking trail is simple and you don't need a guide for the trek. The trek is covered in approximately 40–60 minutes, and that depends on how fast you are.' 'There are no restaurants or food stalls available inside the park; however, small hotels are present at the entrance.' Advance booking required.

facts.topic: Chidiya Tapu — entry fee and sunset-viewing rules
facts.value: 'Beach entry is free.' FAQ: 'The beach and sunset point are free. The Chidiya Tapu Biological Park charges around 20 rupees for Indian visitors and 50 rupees for foreign nationals, with children under 5 free and camera charges extra (as of 2026).' Opening: 'The beach runs on daylight, roughly sunrise to sunset, and the forest road winds down after dark.' 'Reach the sunset point at least 30 minutes before the listed sunset time.' 'Do not arrive after dark or linger too late. The forest road has little lighting and the beach zone effectively winds down by early evening.' Swimming not advised — rocky seabed, strong currents, saltwater crocodiles reported. Mobile network patchy to non-existent. Chidiya Tapu Beach is the main sunset spot; Munda Pahar Beach a few km further is where the trek starts. Cab: sedan Port Blair↔Chidiya Tapu return roughly ₹1,500 (2026); government bus ~₹30 one way, infrequent, does not wait. Distance 25–28 km, 45–60 min. Food: only small stalls near the parking area selling tea, packaged snacks and coconut water; no restaurants at the beach.

facts.topic: Chidiya Tapu Biological Park — ticket, hours, weekly closure
facts.value: Ticket cost from INR 50 (adults), INR 20 (children). Timings 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM. Closed on Monday. Camera fee INR 50 (still), INR 100 (video). Address: Biological Park, Chidiya Tapu, Port Blair, South Andaman. 25 km / 45 minutes from Port Blair. Note this contradicts andamantourism.org, which lists ₹20 Indian / ₹50 foreign.

facts.topic: Baratang — monsoon/September risk to the day trip
facts.value: 'Roughly June to August the day gets genuinely difficult — heavy rain hurts the road, the boats and the cave access — and we'll usually talk you out of it rather than sell it.' September is a workable shoulder month: 'May and September are workable shoulder months: greener, quieter, cheaper, with the odd shower.' Elsewhere: 'Avoid visiting during monsoon (June to September) as heavy rains may delay the convoys and make the trekking path slippery' (Exclusive Andaman); 'the May–September monsoon can suspend the ferry and boat rides at short notice' (TravelTriangle).

facts.topic: Baratang — conduct rules in the Jarawa Reserve
facts.value: No photography or video anywhere in the tribal reserve (strictly enforced, cameras can be confiscated); no stopping and no opening windows during the convoy; no interaction, waving or offering food or items; violations can mean removal from the tour, legal action, fine or imprisonment. All guests must carry a valid government photo ID for verification at the checkpoints.

critical_claims.claim: BARATANG COST MODEL FOR 3 ADULTS — private cab. The cleanest published private-cab breakdown is Dekho Andaman (Port Blair local operator): ₹5,400 for a non-shared Ertiga (max 6 pax + driver) covering Limestone Cave and Mud Volcano, with the vehicle ferry tickets, tolls, parking, driver and the Middle Andaman permit for every traveller INCLUDED, and only meals and the ₹800-per-person Limestone Cave boat excluded. For 3 adults that is ₹5,400 + 3×₹800 = ₹7,800 total (₹2,600 per head) before food.

BARATANG COST MODEL FOR 3 ADULTS — the right vehicle for 3 people is a sedan, and the published sedan round-trip rate is ₹5,000–₹6,500 for the car, with the vehicle ferry at Middle Strait, forest/permit fees, the ₹800–₹1,200 pp shared speedboat, the ₹100–₹300 pp Mud Volcano jeep and all meals payable separately on the spot.

BARATANG COST MODEL FOR 3 ADULTS — shared/joining alternative. A joining tour is ₹2,250 per head (₹6,750 for three), including A/C shared cab with hotel pickup and drop, convoy permit assistance at Jirkatang, shared speedboat tickets and all tolls and parking — but excluding the ₹14 pp vehicle ferry ticket, every meal, the professional cave guide, camera fees and GST. For a party of exactly three this is barely cheaper than a private cab, so the private cab is the better value.

BARATANG COST MODEL FOR 3 ADULTS — permits. Indian nationals pay nothing for a Baratang permit: you carry a government photo ID and register at the Jirkatang forest check post, and the operator or driver handles the convoy paperwork. There is also no entry fee for Baratang Island itself.

BARATANG — the speedboat at Nilambur jetty is the one substantial per-head cost on top of the cab: ₹900–₹1,000 per person, booked at the counter on arrival, for a 6–8 seat motorboat, ~25 minutes each way through the mangrove creek.

BARATANG — return convoy. The last return convoy from the Baratang side is 3:00 PM and missing it strands you; the recent pattern is outbound convoys around 6:00, 9:00 and 11:30 AM. Timings are revised periodically and must be confirmed locally the day before.

BARATANG — return convoy, the source of the 12:00/12:30 confusion. There are multiple southbound slots, not one: the published table gives Baratang→Port Blair returns at approximately 12:00 PM, 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM, against Jirkatang northbound departures of 6:00 AM, 9:00 AM, 12:30 PM and 3:30 PM. So 12:00/12:30 is an early return slot and ~14:30–15:00 is the last one.

SATURDAY CELLULAR JAIL SHOW — on Saturday 26 September 2026 every Light & Sound Show is in HINDI. The official government schedule runs the 5:50 PM and 7:50 PM Hindi shows all days, the 6:50 PM Hindi show on Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday/Sunday, and the 6:50 PM ENGLISH show only on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. The claim that English runs only Mon/Wed/Fri is CONFIRMED.
SATURDAY CELLULAR JAIL SHOW — price is ₹300 per adult (₹900 for three), with children 5–11 at ₹150; this is a separate ticket from the ₹30-per-Indian daytime museum entry.

SATURDAY CELLULAR JAIL SHOW — tickets are bought online on the official Andaman Tourism e-Tourist portal, which is the booking channel linked from the government tourism homepage: register with visitor details, receive an acknowledgement number, choose the visit date and show, pay via SBI ePay, and print the confirmation slip.

SATURDAY CELLULAR JAIL SHOW — the weekday language rule is visible in live data, not just the published table: the portal's 7-day seat grid shows the 06:50 PM English slot as 'No Show' on Saturday 22 August 2026 while both Hindi slots have seats, and shows the reverse on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
MUNDA PAHAD CUT-OFF — entry for the trek closes at 3:00 PM and visitors must be back by 4:15–4:30 PM. The trail is about 1.5 km one way and takes roughly 30–40 minutes; entry is free.

MUNDA PAHAD CUT-OFF — independently corroborated by a second operator, whose fact box reads 'Timings: Approx. 1.5 to 2 km (one way) Till 03:00 PM', with the trail starting at the Chidiya Tapu forest check post and described as a mild 30–40 minute hike, and an explicit warning to trek only in daylight.

MUNDA PAHAD — the slower time estimate is equally well sourced: about 1.5 km one way taking roughly 45 to 60 minutes on an uneven path with a few inclines. Combined with the 30–40 minute readings, budget 30–60 minutes up and 2–2.5 hours round trip including time at the cliff, which means starting no later than about 14:00 to respect the 15:00 gate.

warnings: No government or forest-department source publishes the Andaman Trunk Road convoy schedule online. I searched site:andaman.gov.in and site:tourism.andamannicobar.gov.in for convoy timings and got zero results. Every convoy time in this report comes from tour operators, and they do not fully agree. Operators themselves say the schedule is 'periodically revised' and that they confirm it the day they book. The convoy time must be reconfirmed in Port Blair the day before 26 Sep.

Return-convoy figures genuinely conflict across sources and I could not fully reconcile them: Go2Andaman says returns at 12:00 PM and 3:00 PM; Tropical Andamans says the last return is 3:00 PM; Exclusive Andaman lists a fourth convoy at 3:00 PM; TravelTriangle's table says ~12:00 PM, 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM; Localpostit reports 6:30/9:30/12:30/3:30 from the Mid Strait check post. The most authoritative of these is Tropical Andamans (a Port Blair operator whose page carries an explicit 'last checked 27 July 2026' date and a stated methodology of confirming timings on the day of booking) — treat 15:00 as the hard last return and be at the ferry queue by 13:00.

Dekho Andaman's own page contradicts itself on convoys, stating 'There are two convoys : 8.00 am and 10.00 am' in its notes while its hour-by-hour plan has a 4:00 AM departure reaching Middle Strait by 8:30 AM. Their times bullet is unreliable; their price breakdown appears sound.

Andaman Ocean quotes ₹2,250 per person in its headline and pricing block but ₹2,100 per person in the Terms & Conditions on the same page, and runs a second page at ₹2,100. Get any shared-tour quote in writing before paying.

Whether there is a cave entry ticket is unresolved: TravelTriangle says there is none, ferrybooking.in says ₹5–10 per person at the entry, Andaman Ocean bundles unspecified 'entry tickets'. Immaterial to the budget but do not be surprised by a small counter charge.

Chidiya Tapu Biological Park entry fee conflicts between sources: andamantourism.org says ₹20 Indian / ₹50 foreign, Go2Andaman says from ₹50 adults / ₹20 children. Both agree on 9 AM–4 PM and a Monday closure. Not relevant for a Saturday, but confirm at the gate.

The Munda Pahad 15:00 cut-off rests on two travel sites, neither a government source, and one of them (andamansguide.com) carries its own disclaimer that it is not the official Andaman government website. I found no forest-department notification. Also, andamansguide gives Chidiya Tapu as 17 km from Port Blair, which conflicts with the 25–30 km given by every other source including Go2Andaman, Experience Andamans and andamantourism.org — that page is loose with numbers, and it also internally contradicts itself (1.5 km trek in one place, 2 km in another).

26 September 2026 falls at the tail of the monsoon. Multiple operators warn that from roughly June to September heavy rain can suspend the Baratang creek boats and make the cave trail slippery, and that convoys can be delayed. Tropical Andamans calls September a 'workable shoulder month' but says of June–August that they would 'talk you out of it rather than sell it'. Build in a fallback day and confirm the boat is running.

iAndaman.com lists a ₹600 per head boat fare and states 'Days Open/Closed: Closed: Monday' for Baratang — that page's copyright line reads 2017 and both claims are contradicted by every current source. I did not rely on it.

I found no published statement on whether Cellular Jail Light & Sound Show tickets can be bought at an on-site counter, nor how far in advance online booking opens. The official portal's availability grid only publishes 7 days ahead, so 26 Sep 2026 was not yet listed on 20 Aug 2026. Mark both as UNKNOWN; the official helpdesk numbers are +91 3192 232694 and +91 3192 230933, office hours 8:30 AM–5:00 PM Mon–Sat.
I did not fill in, submit or pay through the e-Tourist registration form, and did not log in anywhere. All figures were read from published pages only.

Three domains blocked page-text extraction and had to be read via screenshots (andamanocean.in, dekhoandaman.com, acquaintandaman.com); azuretrailsandaman.in, enclaveandaman.com, travelourister.com and rartoursandtravel.com would not load at all. Facts from the screenshot-read pages are transcribed from the rendered page.

Some operator pages consulted (notably eandamantourism.com and trekgo.in) read as generically written content rather than first-hand local knowledge, with round-number ranges and hedged language. I have preferred Tropical Andamans, Dekho Andaman, Andaman Ocean, Go2Andaman and Experience Andamans, which publish specific, checkable figures and dated verification.
